Samir: Quick sync — proposing a slice-based head/tail sampling approach for OTLP spans to cut telemetry cost while keeping high-fidelity traces for trouble windows. Idea: always keep the head (first N ms or first X spans), then apply a weighted tail sample by route + customer tier. Anya: Can you sketch the decision rules? how do we map route+tier -> weight? also are we preserving sampled traces for error cases? :thinking_face: Samir: Short version: - Head: keep full-span sequence for the first 200ms (configurable HEAD_MS) or first 5 spans of a trace. - Tail: after head threshold, compute weight = base_for_route * tier_multiplier. Base_for_route from historical error/latency heatmap; tier_multiplier = {enterprise: 1.0, pro: 0.5, free: 0.1}. - Always keep if span has error tag or status != OK. Liam: That sounds reasonable. Two quick ops questions: 1) How do exporters see the sampling decision? 2) How do we guarantee unbiased metrics for spans we downsample? Samir: Exporters should get an explicit sampling.meta attached to root span: `sampling.mode=H/T`, `sampling.weight=

`, `sampling.reason=route-heatmap` and `sampling.decider=runtime`. That way downstream storages can reconstruct or adjust counts. For metrics we plan to emit `span_ingested{route, tier, sampled=true/false}` counters so dashboards can extrapolate. Maya: Ops: retention + cost. If we keep head for many traces, tail sampling cut needs to be aggressive. Suggest adding a global budget per-customer (tokens/day) with soft quota alerts in the Console. Route weights should be normalized to meet budget. Anya: For the heatmap, do we compute base_for_route offline in telemetry pipeline or use a streaming estimator? Samir: Prototype = offline once/day. Long-term = streaming estimator in the router (per-route EWMA of error rate and p50/p95 latency). The router exposes an endpoint `/sampling-profile/` so the sampler can query weights. Runtime config + canary in Console for toggling. Liam: Implementation note: keep sampling logic idempotent and side-effect free at the span emitter. e.g. attach `sampling.score` metric then let a centralized sampler decide (helps SDKs + envs where we can't query the router). Samir: Draft pseudo-code I posted to the PR: ```python def should_keep_root(span): if span.has_error(): return True if span.duration_ms <= HEAD_MS or span.span_index < HEAD_SPANS: return True weight = get_route_weight(span.route, span.tenant_tier) return random.random() < weight ``` Maya: UX question: Console needs a human-friendly view: per-route sampling % (head vs tail), estimations of bytes saved, and expected ingestion per-day per-tenant. Also a canary toggle per-route to gradually reduce tail weights. Anya: Tests: we need deterministic tests for boundary conditions (exactly HEAD_MS, error flags, tier mapping). Also a simulation harness to run historical traces through sampler and show expected storage reduction + SLO coverage. Samir: Agreed. I'll open an RFC that includes: sampling model, exporter attrs, console endpoints, and a small simulation dataset. Plan to ship a limited beta for a handful of enterprise customers first. telemetry-bot: experiment-started: "slice-tail-sampling/proto-v1" by Samir at 1789002000 Liam: One more: make sure OTLP exporter preserves original trace IDs and includes `sampling.meta` so downstream APM UIs can link sampled tails back to heads (if head spans are in short-term store and tails in cheaper long-term store). Samir: Yep. I'll add the attributes and a runbook for emergency disable (console toggle + infra flag). PR incoming this afternoon. :rocket:
